package_info.why_malicious: Attackers inserted malicious code into the SolarWinds Orion software update process, resulting in a supply chain attack that distributed backdoored software to thousands of customers. The malicious code enabled remote access and data exfiltration from victim environments.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (on service start or update install)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The code establishes a covert communication channel to attacker-controlled servers, beacons out, and awaits further instructions. It can download and execute additional payloads, exfiltrate data, and perform lateral movement.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is hidden within a legitimate DLL and only activates under certain conditions to avoid detection. It establishes outbound network connections to remote servers unrelated to SolarWinds operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Orion software should not contain code that beacons to external servers or executes remote commands. Software updates should not introduce hidden backdoors.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may beacon to central servers, but only with user consent and clear documentation.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code in a core business DLL
Outbound network connections to suspicious domains

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is inserted into the SolarWinds Orion update DLL during the build process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Distribution of backdoored software to customers

attack_chain.action: Customers install the compromised update, loading the malicious DLL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in customer environments

attack_chain.action: Malicious code beacons to attacker-controlled servers and awaits instructions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote command execution, data exfiltration, and lateral movement

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion Core BusinessLayerHost process
DLLs with obfuscated or anomalous code in Orion installation directory
Conditional execution logic to evade sandboxes or debugging
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with hash not matching official release
Presence of unknown or modified DLLs in Orion software directories
network_indicators: Connections to known Sunburst C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com)
Unusual DNS queries or HTTP/S traffic from Orion servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected outbound network connections from SolarWinds Orion processes, especially to known C2 domains. Validate the integrity of Orion DLLs against official hashes. Use EDR or AV tools to detect obfuscated or suspicious code within Orion binaries. Monitor for process behaviors such as spawning unexpected child processes or accessing sensitive files.
